title: Китайская экскурсия и обещание Макса  (The Chinese Tour Group and Max's Promise)

segments.t: Vika rushes into the kitchen in a panic to tell Max that an entire busload of Chinese tourists has just sat down expecting lunch while the Chef is gone and Lyova is on vacation. As Vika grabs her phone to call Nagiyev, Max begs her to trust him to save the service.
Шеф уехал, су-шеф в отпуске, а остальные...
Let's replay the exchange and look closely at each Russian phrase.

'We have guests in the dining room.' Barinov explains that they have guests in the dining room, keeping his voice calm and direct. Russian expresses having something as "by me is", keeping the phrase short and grounded.
'There was supposed to be one and a half people today.' Realizing that there was supposed to be one and a half people today changes how Vika handles the situation.
'A whole tour group just arrived.' With the trust and promise in play, Nagiyev keeps this short reply brisk and direct.

'Do you understand what kind of situation this is?' Here asking whether Nagiyev understands what kind of situation this is shows Barinov looking for the real truth. In Russian, he does not need helper words like "do" or "did"—rising pitch alone turns it into a question.
Шеф уехал, су-шеф в отпуске, а остальные...
'The Chef left, the sous-chef is on vacation, and the rest...' Admitting that the Chef left the is on vacation and the rest shows Vika being honest for a change.
'Wait, why is that?' With the work and phone hanging in the air, Nagiyev puts Barinov on the spot.

'Have you all lost your minds?' Here asking whether Nagiyev all lost Nagiyev's minds shows Barinov looking for the real truth. Notice how he sticks to the formal "you", keeping a professional line between them.
'The acting sous-chef is right here on duty.' Adding that the acting is right here on duty fills in the missing piece for Barinov.
'Alright, that is it.' Nagiyev tells Barinov that Alright that is it without dressing it up.
'I am calling Dmitriy Vladimirovich right now.' Being calling Dmitriy Vladimirovich right now moves the conversation forward without extra drama.

'Vika, please do not.' With the shift and phone in play, Vika keeps this short reply brisk and direct. There is no "you" needed in the Russian here: one short word states the rule for everyone in the room.
'Vika, I will solve this problem myself.' Saying that he will solve this problem himself is how Nagiyev sets the tone with Barinov.
'Trust me, please.' Since Nagiyev should trust him please, Barinov does not waste words on excuses. Let's hear the complete conversation once more.
Шеф уехал, су-шеф в отпуске, а остальные...

That wraps up this scene as with the dining room packed with Chinese tourists and the kitchen short-staffed, Vika reaches for the phone to call Nagiyev, but Max begs her to let him solve the crisis. Until next time!
